title: Sequence: Blocks in Order
description: The simplest shape of all: do this, then this, then this. Build your first real program and drive a robot through a maze.

content.value: A sequence is nothing more than a list of steps, run top to bottom, one after another. It sounds almost too simple to teach — until you notice that swapping the order of two steps can produce a completely different result. "Turn right, then move forward" and "move forward, then turn right" send a robot to two different places.

content.title: 🧩 Drive to the flag
content.hint: Stack Move forward, Turn left and Turn right blocks in order to get from the start to the 🏁.

content.value: There's no trick to this maze — it just needs the right steps in the right order, one block at a time. Notice how many blocks it took. The next lesson introduces a way to say "repeat this part" instead of writing it out by hand every time, which is exactly the kind of thing that starts to matter once a sequence gets long.

This exact idea — instructions running one after another — is what every one of ARIA's real Python programs will do too, starting next module. Blocks just make the order visible as a physical stack instead of lines of text.
Key takeaway: a sequence runs steps in the exact order they're stacked. Getting the order right is often the entire challenge, even with completely correct individual steps.

quiz.question: A robot is told "turn right, then move forward" instead of "move forward, then turn right." What's true about these two sequences?
options: They can send the robot to two different places, since order changes the result
The second one is always faster
quiz.explain: The exact same two steps, reordered, take the robot somewhere different — order is part of what a sequence means.

quiz.question: What does a sequence block program actually do, mechanically?
options: Runs every block at the same time
Runs the stacked blocks in order, top to bottom
Picks a random block to run first
quiz.explain: That's the entire definition of a sequence — one step after another, in the order written.
